No one said it was a Casino. But this boxes are very much a gamble mechanic. This game isn't alone in it, in fact most freemium games have gamble mechanics like this one. Japan even has a law where mechanics like this have to show the % of obtaining x item due to gambling. Sadly North America doesn't so we are left in the blind. For the record, I don't think there's a single person that disagrees with what your post was about. And I personally DO NOT support this type of mechanics. Do i think me not buying this boxes sends a message? sure. Do i think anything will change? no. Why? Because this type of games attract "whales" who go all in in stuff like this. The whole point of my post was to explain to you what the boxes are. They aren't meant to provide a discount for your money. ie: Only items worth 95 shards or more. They are meant to raise the ceiling of their maximum profits. Going by your scenario if they had 10 items at a max of 950 with no filler. Then people would either buy all for 950 or enough till they get what they want. That said, it has the side effect of very clearly becoming a "pay2win" scenario and on top of that it has a ripple effect on the tunning of the event and their profits from other stuff such as people who buy this stuff potentially not speeding up stuff anymore, not paying shards for film, octobots etc. By doing it the way they are doing, they seek to get a higher "average" profit due to the people spending more money than they would otherwise. It might sound very dramatic, but this is indeed gambling and its a psychological trap to get you to think you "win" when you get stuff that would be worth more than 95 shards and have another go. Eventually even if you bought all boxes to get what you wanted you end up with a feeling of "Oh well, at least i'm set for this item and this item and I can use this item to buy this thing, and I didn't want this bobblehead but at least the collection is complete. And hey I got my costume!"
